record.paper_title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions
record.context_brief: Extracting eta-nucleus scattering from production data
record.original_question: How can scattering lengths or other eta-nucleus scattering parameters be quantitatively and reliably extracted from eta-production data when final-state interactions, effective-range corrections, and inelastic channels are present? A solution should go beyond using the Watson-Migdal scattering-length formula only qualitatively, because the direct proportionality between production and elastic scattering energy dependences holds only when the scattering length is much larger than the effective range, and because no closed-form final-state-interaction expression is available in the presence of inelasticities.

evidence.quote: Note that one should be careful in interpreting the value of a extracted from a fit to production data as the scattering length.

However, a direct proportionality between the energy dependence of scattering and production only holds, if the scattering length is significantly larger than the next term in the effective range expansion — the effective range.

One should also stress that in the presence of inelasticities it is not even possible to derive an expression for the final state interaction effect in closed form. Thus the results should be taken on a qualitative level.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the production reaction A + B → η + X, where η denotes the eta meson and X denotes a nuclear final state, measured near the η-X production threshold. Let q denote the relative η-X momentum in the final state, and let f_η(q) be the η-X elastic scattering amplitude with low-energy expansion

   q cot δ(q) = 1/a + (1/2) r_0 q^2 + O(q^4),

where a is the (in general complex) η-X scattering length and r_0 is the effective range. The Watson–Migdal prescription approximates the production amplitude as M(q) ≈ M_0 · f_η(q), giving a direct proportionality between the energy dependence of the production cross section and that of elastic η-X scattering only when |a| is much larger than |r_0|.

Develop a quantitative and reliable method to extract the η-X scattering parameters (scattering length a, effective range r_0, and analogous complex low-energy parameters) from measured η-production data subject to the following complications simultaneously:

   (i) The final-state η-X interaction must be included beyond the leading scattering-length approximation, accounting for effective-range corrections when |a| and |r_0| are comparable.
   (ii) Inelastic channels (e.g., πN, ππN openings coupled to ηN, or breakup channels for nuclear targets) are open at the relevant energies, so that no closed-form Watson–Migdal-type final-state interaction factor is known.
   (iii) The production operator (the "short-distance" part M_0) may itself depend on q and must be disentangled from the final-state interaction in a controlled, model-independent way.

The problem is to construct such an extraction scheme and to quantify rigorously the theoretical uncertainty it incurs on a and r_0.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., reviews on η-nucleus interactions through 2013 and analyses of γd → π⁰ηd through 2022) continues to report scattering-length determinations with significant model-dependence and large uncertainties, with different K-matrix and coupled-channel approaches yielding incompatible values (real parts ranging from ~0.2 fm to ~0.9 fm). No closed-form, model-independent extraction handling effective-range corrections together with inelasticities has been established; the problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Interaction of eta mesons with nuclei (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Different theoretical approaches yield η-N scattering lengths such as 0.20+i0.26 fm, 0.26+i0.25 fm, 0.18+i0.42 fm, and 0.91+i0.27 fm.
status_evidence.claim: Wide spread in extracted η-N scattering lengths persists, indicating no consensus method.

status_evidence.title: The γd → π0ηd reaction and extraction of the ηd scattering length
status_evidence.snippet: The major source of uncertainty is associated with the production mechanism and off-shell contributions to the η-d interaction.
status_evidence.claim: Recent extractions still rely on model-dependent production mechanisms with substantial uncertainty.

status_evidence.title: η-Nucleon scattering length and effective range uncertainties
status_evidence.snippet: K-matrix fits give a=0.75-i0.27 fm and r0=-1.50-i0.24 fm, with significant uncertainties from coupled channels.
status_evidence.claim: Effective-range parameters are comparable in magnitude to the scattering length, undermining the Watson–Migdal leading approximation.
